title: The palette is read from the Omarchy theme at start
body:
`decade-ui/src/palette.rs` holds 26 colours as `pub const` values, which drawing code names directly in about 163 places. Thirteen are a hardcoded copy of the colours in Omarchy's `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml` as of 2026-11-06. Twelve were picked by hand as shades of those, and `SHADOW` is a fixed black. A theme switch in Omarchy does not reach decade.

## Proposal

- At start, each process reads `colors.toml` from its own machine. When the file or a key is missing, the process uses today's values. A viewer on another machine therefore reads its own theme, or falls back.
- The palette holds the theme keys decade uses, under the theme's names. A global holds the palette, and the process sets it once at start. Drawing code reads colours from it, and tests see today's values.
- The twelve hand-picked shades become blends of theme colours, with the `mix` that `palette.rs` already has. The amounts are fitted to today's values, so the current theme looks almost the same:

| today | becomes |
|---|---|
| `DARK_RED`, `DARK_YELLOW`, `DARK_GREEN` | 15% of the way from `background` to the colour |
| `MID_RED`, `MID_YELLOW`, `MID_GREEN` | 28% of the way from `background` to the colour |
| `LIGHT_RED`, `LIGHT_YELLOW`, `LIGHT_GREEN` | 45% of the way from the colour to `foreground` |
| `FADED_FOREGROUND` | 15% of the way from `foreground` to `background` |
| `RAISED_BACKGROUND` | 15% of the way from `background` to `lighter_background` |
| `BORDER` | a third of the way from `selection` to `muted` |

Jack compared today's palette, theme keys alone, and theme keys with these blends in a mockup, `figures/decade-palette.acre` in the acre repository. He judged all three close, and chose the blends.

## Rejected

- Theme keys alone, with `bright_*` for the light text, `selection` for `BORDER` and `background` for `RAISED_BACKGROUND`. The mockup showed it a little worse than the blends.
- A `Palette` value passed to every drawing function. It changes most of the chrome's signatures, and a process reads the theme only once.
- The server sending its palette to viewers. Every viewer runs on the server's machine today. A remote viewer, decade-e3a784, can add that when it changes the protocol.

## Out of scope

- Reloading on a theme change. Omarchy's theme-set hooks could restart or signal decade later.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/5da9dd6b
notes.text: Not started; the spec leaves three things open that change the look or the design. (1) Twelve palette names have no key in colors.toml: FADED_FOREGROUND, LIGHT_RED/YELLOW/GREEN, DARK_RED/YELLOW/GREEN, MID_RED/YELLOW/GREEN, RAISED_BACKGROUND, BORDER (SHADOW is a fixed black). They must be derived from theme keys (mix toward foreground or background?) or stay fixed; fixed values clash with a different theme. (2) decade-ui's palette is pub consts (163 uses, plus const aliases in frame.rs and panes.rs). Runtime colours need a loaded Palette value or a once-set global; which one is a design choice. (3) A viewer on another machine draws chrome, so the server must send the palette over the wire or the viewer reads its own file; the spec does not say which.
